recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-39122; future _maxresults refinements should be handled under later Jira decisions such as FHIR-46763 or new WG-approved tickets.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive R5 FHIR-core search issue asking whether a client can indicate it only needs the first few search results so a server need not prepare later pages; the accepted resolution was to add a parameter for this, recorded as _maxResults in Jira/minutes and implemented as _maxresults.
initial_application: Git commit 31975a04ec83f6394a0d5e542fb36069f782e9d6 explicitly applied FHIR-39122 by adding _maxresults to source/search.html's contents navigation, search-result parameter table, Limiting Total Result Size section, and summary table. The current source retains those entries.
additional_context: The Jira-linked Zulip thread clarified that _count limits page size while the requested feature limits total results and avoids unnecessary server paging state. FHIR-I minutes from 2023-02-13 record a Persuasive 16-0-1 vote and suggested the _maxResults name. The R5 and current CI published pages consistently expose the implemented lower-case _maxresults spelling. Later FHIR-46763 clarified that _maxresults applies only to match entries, and that related issue already has a combined-branch audit commit.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because source/search.html already contains the necessary build-scoped documentation for _maxresults and no current semantic gap remains for FHIR-39122.

related_jiras.note: Clarified that _maxresults limits match entries and not included/outcome resources; already represented on the combined branch, so no duplicate opportunistic commit was published.
